analytic.title: Guaranteeing Fault Tolerance in Real Time Systems under Error Bursts

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Real-time systems in dynamic environments can encounter faults that can lead to incorrect computation resulting in failure of system or exhibit degraded system performance. Earlier studies focused on managing systems susceptible to faults especially due to error bursts caused by environment exposure and can be disastrous. It is important to deploy strategies to guarantee schedulability of these systems using temporal redundancy for such error bursts. This research employs a methodology for determining upper bound margin of a fault burst model with Rate Monotonic (RM) scheduling, provide error recovery strategy under error bursts, worst case response time (WCRT) and scheduling feasibility. Analysis with a given task set shows the fault tolerant schedulability and an algorithm has been developed for schedulability under various fault burst durations. Evaluation with performance traces and WCRT have been carried out with GUI in MATLAB. This work can be extended to multiprocessor systems, tolerating multiple error bursts and spatial redundancy for safety critical systems.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Real time systems are systems in which the correctness of the system not only depends on the output but also on the timeliness in which it is obtained. Many real time systems operate in harsh conditions which require strict adhesion to task deadlines. Some of the examples of real-time systems include fly-by-wire aircraft, space shuttles, industrial hazard monitoring system, automobiles and road traffic monitoring systems. Scheduling policies in real-time systems need to guarantee that tasks will meet their deadlines in all circumstances, even in the presence of permanent, transient or intermittent faults.

Transient faults such as error bursts that occur due to high intensity radiated fields near radar stations can exist for unknown duration [1]. Error recovery method has been employed to tolerate faults due to error bursts and it is found that the strategy guarantees scheduling with fault tolerance under error bursts. Checkpointing has been used to achieve timeliness in real time systems under error burst [2].

A fault model has been introduced to depict error burst in the environment where it is depicted as a temporal distribution of faults [2]. This error burst is assumed to have a bounded time interval. This paper introduces a scheduling policy which integrates rate monotonic scheduling with unit checkpointing and an error recovery strategy to achieve fault tolerance. Schedulability of the taskset is guaranteed using the condition that worst case response time of tasks must always be less than or equal to task deadline. Evaluation of the algorithm is demonstrated for a generic taskset and a GUI is developed for performance traces and metrics.

Section II of the paper deals with literature survey and background study. System overview and approach has been described in section III. Simulation and evaluation is given in section IV along with GUI in MATLAB. The last section deals with conclusion and future scope of this research.

div.head: II. LITERATURE SURVEY AND BACKGROUND STUDY
div.p: Fault tolerant real time system can be viewed as one that must deliver the expected service in a timely manner even in the presence of faults as stated in [1] by Shin and Ramanathan. For example, antilock braking in automobile system must be activated the instant a wheel lock is detected. Aysan in [2] has stated that fault is the cause of an error. The faults are categorized into internal and external faults based on the system boundaries and based on their level of persistence, further divided into permanent, transient and intermittent faults. Errors that occur for a period of time cannot be considered as singleton events as they may not be realistic in nature. Abhilash in [3] defines error bursts as series of soft, transient or intermittent errors that occurs for a known duration preventing successful task executions. Computer systems comprising of CPU, memory or other I/O subsystems operating in airport areas may be affected by error bursts due to electromagnetic waves produced by radar.

Electromagnetic interference (EMI) can cause error bursts which may lead to transmission errors in controller area network of automotive fields [4]. A real time system is said to be fault tolerant if it is capable of scheduling tasks even in the worst case scenarios under a predefined fault hypothesis [5]. The feasibility of critical tasks of the real time systems under error burst should be guaranteed and also that of non critical tasks should be guaranteed [6]. Resource augmentations can guarantee fault tolerance feasibility in uniprocessor systems under error burst [7]. Simple task reexecution can handle various intermittent, transient, hardware and software faults whereas permanent faults can be tolerated by providing an additional set of processors to execute periodic tasks in an independent manner [8]. Aysan [9] has stated that spatial and temporal redundancy are used to achieve fault tolerance feasibility in safety critical applications.

Error burst model has been introduced in [10] and various strategies to recover from these faults are provided to guarantee fault tolerance. End Detection/Full Re-execution/Simple and End Detection/Full Re-execution/Multiple are two error recovery strategies mentioned in [10]. Checkpointing is a technique to reduce overall computation time of tasks in systems affected by faults. When overall checkpointing cost does not change with time, optimal strategy is to use checkpointing with fixed intervals [11].

div.head: III. SYSTEM OVERVIEW
div.p: Section A of system overview introduces task model. System model and error burst model is given in section B and C. Assumptions made in the algorithm are explained in section D. Section E and F deals with fault tolerant RM scheduling and fault free response time.

div.head: A. Task Model
div.p: Tasks in the task model are assumed to be periodic and independent in nature. Computation time and period of each task in the taskset is represented by and , respectively. All tasks in the taskset are released at the first instant of period and consumes units for its execution. The deadline of each task is equal to its period .

div.head: B. System Model
div.p: Uniprocessor platform is considered for the system model in this paper. A uniprocessor achieves its expected service by executing a set sequence of tasks in order. Suitable scheduling algorithms are used to schedule tasks on a uniprocessor system.

Rate monotonic (RM) scheduling algorithm is considered to schedule the tasks in the proposed system. Tasks with shorter time periods are given highest priority in RM scheduling. Independent tasks are assumed to avoid resource sharing.

div.head: C. Error Burst Model
div.p: Fault tolerant scheduling algorithms must guarantee schedulability of all tasks in taskset under faulty conditions. No system can tolerate any random set of faults within a definite time interval [12]. An error burst model must be defined to guarantee schedulability in fault tolerant systems. [9] is shown in Fig. 1. In this model, error burst of duration is defined during which error distribution is unknown. Separation between error burst is assumed to be at least units. This model is accepted based on the assumption that no faults occur outside the fault duration ( ).

div.head: D. Assumptions
div.p: • Error bursts occur for unknown durations during which the error distribution is undefined. • It is assumed that error bursts will occur only once within a hyperperiod of the taskset. • Real time system is assumed to have inherent fault detection mechanisms like acceptance tests and watchdog timers. • Checkpointing cost is assumed to be negligible for the real time system. • Operating system and scheduler are assumed to remain unaffected by error burst and executes error recovery strategy. • Instantaneous fault detection and reexecution takes place in the system.

div.head: E. Fault Tolerant RM Scheduling
div.p: Error bursts can stall or completely corrupt execution of task instances in real time systems. Once an error detection mechanism within the system detects an error burst, task recovery strategy is initiated by operating system to recover faulty instants of task.

Fault tolerant real time system has been achieved by RM scheduling with error recovery strategy. The error recovery strategy used is task reexecution. Checkpointing at fixed intervals allow faulty instants of tasks affected by error bursts to be reexecuted. Tasks are scheduled in the system by fault tolerant RM scheduling such that no deadline miss occurs for the taskset. Response time of tasks give an insight to whether tasks are schedulable by RM scheduling algorithm.

div.head: F. Fault Free Response Time
div.p: Response time of task computed in absence of fault is termed as fault free response time . Calculation of involves consideration of release of all higher priority tasks when execution of lower priority task is still in progress.

div.head: G. Error Burst Response Time
div.p: All task executions are affected when an error burst occurs in the system. Response time of tasks under error burst has been represented by . Error burst response time of task has been expressed as the sum of fault free response time , error burst duration , interferences
due to preemptions by higher priority tasks and a factor representing error recovery strategy. All preemptions due to faulty task under error burst are integrated in the term .

Any error recovery strategy involves mainly error detection and correction which consumes additional time. The term represents this additional time consumed by error recovery strategy. Error burst response time of a task should be less than its absolute deadline to attain schedulablility by RM scheduling algorithm.
Task reexecution is used as an error recovery strategy to attain fault tolerant RM scheduling. Reexecution of only faulty task instances are performed ensuring all deadlines are strictly met.

div.head: IV. SIMULATION AND EVALUATION
div.p: RM scheduling of a given input taskset without error burst is given in section A. The next section B describes RM scheduling with error burst with and without fault tolerance. Also the upper bound margins for the error burst duration have been determined. Performance evaluation of the algorithm with results has been given in section C.

div.head: A. Schedulability of Input Taskset
div.p: The proposed algorithm is simulated using four tasks provided in taskset Table I. All timing parameters are in time units. RM scheduling trace of the given input taskset is given in Fig. 2. Scheduling trace has been plotted for one hyperperiod of the input taskset. Given input taskset has hyperperiod of 300 time units. Upper bound on error burst duration ( ) for various tasks in the taskset has been analyzed and is shown in Table I. Minimum error burst duration for the given input taskset is 28 time units. All error bursts of duration less than or equal to 28 time units will be tolerated by the fault tolerant (FT) RM scheduling algorithm.

div.head: B. Scheduling under Error Burst
div.p: An error burst of duration =20 time units is generated and injected into the system at 90 time unit. RM scheduling without fault tolerance under said error burst duration is shown in Fig. 3. Fourth instant of Task1, third instant of Task2 and second instant of Task4 are affected by error burst. Results of task instants under error burst duration are lost. Fault Tolerant (FT) RM scheduling of the given input taskset with error burst duration =20 time units is given in Fig. 4. Upper bound on error burst duration is 28 time units. Scheduling tasks with error burst duration more than 28 time units will result in erroneous output.

div.head: C. Performance Evaluation
div.p: Scheduling is done for RM and scheduling trace has been obtained. Error burst of known duration units is injected by the user, scheduling and trace obtained for FTRM. WCRT for both has been given in Table II. The response time of the least priority task is worst affected under error burst. Task4 is the least priority task with 33 time units difference in its response time with and without error burst. The highest priority task is least affected by error bursts as shown in Fig. 6. Time difference observed in highest priority Task1 for the given input taskset is 22 time units. Increase in processor utilization is observed for tasks under error burst. Highest priority task consumes most of system resources. Resource consumption of least priority task is minimal. Still a notable difference is observed in utilization of lower priority tasks under error burst as observed in Fig. 7.

div.head: CONCLUSION
div.p: An algorithm has been developed for fault tolerant RM scheduling under error burst. The fault tolerant scheduling algorithm allows for re-execution of the remainder of the task from the instant at which the fault has occurred. Checkpointing maintains timeliness of the system. Algorithm simulated in MATLAB with scheduling traces and WCRT has been evaluated. The scheduling feasibility of the given taskset has been determined and the GUI gives performance evaluation for the given input.

More studies can be done to determine the feasibility impact based on the instances at which error burst is injected. Also occurrence of multiple error bursts need to be studied. This work can be extended to multiprocessor systems with multiple error bursts and safety critical systems with hardware redundancy.
